page.title: Corpus
page.purpose: Let an operator browse collections and documents, see at a glance where each document was processed and how confident the parse was, and pick up the ones that need human attention.

priorities.statement: Where a document was processed is visible in the list itself, never behind a click.
priorities.notes: Locality is a first-class property of every row. The product claim is falsifiable, so the evidence has to be in the default view.

priorities.statement: A collection's privacy class is visible before anything is added to it.
priorities.notes: The collection confers a default class its documents inherit; a user must see what they are about to inherit.

priorities.statement: Low-confidence parses surface as work, not as silent wrong answers.
Search returns anchored units, and every result can be opened at its exact source region.

states.description: Collections and documents are listed with locality, privacy class and confidence visible.
No collections exist yet; the primary action is creating one, which requires choosing a default privacy class.
A retrieval query is in flight.
Retrieval results are shown, each carrying a resolvable anchor.
The queue of low-confidence parses is filtered into view.
The corpus or retrieval call failed and the reason is visible.

elements.name: Collections
elements.description: Each row shows the collection's default privacy class.

elements.name: Documents
elements.description: Columns include privacy class, where processed, derivation tier and parse confidence.

elements.name: Where processed
elements.description: Local or remote, conveyed by text and shape as well as color.

claims.statement: The corpus page exposes a named browsing region.
Every document row shows where it was processed without the operator opening it.
The local-versus-remote distinction is conveyed by text and shape, never by color alone.
claims.rationale: The residency claim is the product. A user with a color-vision difference must be able to read it, and WCAG 2.1 AA requires it.

claims.statement: Every retrieval result exposes a link that opens the Reader at its exact source region.
claims.rationale: A result the operator cannot trace back to a page is not a citation, and citability is why retrieval exists here at all.

claims.statement: Creating a collection requires choosing a default privacy class; there is no unclassified path.
claims.rationale: OT-P0-025. An unclassified collection would let documents enter with no routing profile, which is the silent failure the guarantee exists to prevent.

claims.statement: Loading, empty, populated and error states are all reachable and distinct.
Search, collection navigation and the review queue are reachable by keyboard alone.
